name: Tasting Australia
reason: Rule 4: a recurring food festival, not a permanent place.
objection: Tourism board promotes it, but an event is only mentioned in best-time text.

name: Port Adelaide
reason: Wikivoyage gives the historic port district its own page: maritime and railway museums, lighthouse, waterfront and dolphin sanctuary cruises; a district visitors base a half day in (rule 1, 2).
objection: Could be a wrapper around its own museums; the proposer decides whether it is a spot or a destination.

name: Port Adelaide Lighthouse
reason: One Wikivoyage entry: 25 m 1869 lighthouse relocated to the waterfront, an exhibit of the Maritime Museum.
objection: Case for: a named landmark in a visitor guide. Against: lit Saturdays only, a short exterior look, part of the Port Adelaide precinct.

name: South Australian Aviation Museum
reason: Wikivoyage lists two hangars of aircraft with guided tours, daily opening, paid entry: a visit well over half an hour (rule 2).
objection: One counted source only; Port Adelaide has several museums and this is a niche one.

name: Hart's Mill Complex
reason: Rule 2: a working flour mill; Wikivoyage describes only buildings, no visitor access or activity.
objection: Heritage waterfront buildings might be a stop on a walking route, but no source says so.

name: Port Adelaide Historical Society Museum
reason: One tourism board listing for a volunteer local history museum.
objection: Case for: a counted source and a free-ish indoor stop. Against: small local museum with Port Adelaide's larger Maritime and Railway museums beside it; opening hours limited.

name: Port River Cruises
reason: Operator/cruise, not a place (COVERAGE: a spot is a place); the place is the Adelaide Dolphin Sanctuary.
objection: The sanctuary is the draw and has no landing point, so it may need to be entered via the sanctuary, not this operator.

name: Fishermen's Wharf Market
reason: Rule 4: a Sunday-only weekly market; no counted source.
objection: It is a long-running Port Adelaide fixture, but weekly markets are excluded.

name: Semaphore Beach
reason: Tourism board attraction page; Wikivoyage names Semaphore's tourist precinct, jetty and beach as an Adelaide seaside outing (rule 1, 2).
objection: Overlaps the Semaphore suburb as a place; it is the same stop, so list once.

name: Largs Bay
reason: No counted source (rule 1); a beach suburb jetty adjacent to Semaphore.
objection: A genuine historic jetty beach; may have a guide listing the script missed.

name: Tennyson Dunes
reason: Wikivoyage and the parks agency name it as the state's most accessible intact dune system, with a walk to do (rule 1, 2).
objection: Short, local-feeling reserve; two counted sources and a half-hour walk carry it.

name: Thompson Beach
reason: One Wikivoyage entry names it as a birdwatching spot of the Bird Sanctuary park.
objection: Case for: samphire coast, shorebird migration. Against: Wikivoyage entry is thin; sits inside the Adelaide International Bird Sanctuary and may be part of that park's spot.

name: Garden Island Ships' Graveyard
reason: Seen only from cruises (Wikivoyage); the wrecks have no visitor access, so rule 2 and the operator rule fail.
objection: Ship graveyards are a popular curiosity; a lookout or boat ramp access could change this.

name: Glenelg Jetty
reason: Two counted sources (tourism board and Wikivoyage's Adelaide guide) but it is the beach's own jetty.
objection: Case for: the classic Glenelg promenade stop. Against: near-duplicate of Glenelg/Glenelg Beach, which is listed elsewhere.

name: Marina Pier Glenelg
reason: Rule 3: part of the Holdfast Shores marina, a near-duplicate of Glenelg; shops and moorings rather than a draw.
objection: Tourism board lists it, but no visitor activity beyond a promenade.

name: Bay Discovery Centre
reason: Wikivoyage names this local museum in Glenelg Town Hall.
objection: Case for: indoor museum of the bay's history, half hour or more. Against: one source, small local museum.

name: The Beachouse
reason: Wikivoyage lists this seafront amusement park (mini-golf, rides, carousel).
objection: Case for: a permanent family attraction on the Glenelg foreshore. Against: a commercial amusement operator with one source, ordinary child attractions.

name: Luna Park Glenelg
reason: Rule 2: the candidate is a former park, closed; no counted source.
objection: None; it is gone.

name: Grange
reason: Wikivoyage only lists the Grange jetty for fishing among suburban beaches; nothing to see or do named beyond that.
objection: Grange jetty and beach are pleasant, but a suburb is not a distinct draw.

name: Brighton
reason: Wikivoyage names Brighton as a beach reached by the Seaford line; jetty and beach.
objection: Case for: one of Adelaide's well-known swimming beaches. Against: only a transport mention and a fishing-jetty line.

name: Brighton Jetty
reason: Duplicate of Brighton (same wiki article, same beach and jetty).
objection: Brighton Jetty is a separate photo stop, but it is one place with the beach.

name: Seacliff
reason: No counted source (rule 1); a suburban beach.
objection: Seacliff has a sheltered beach but no source calls it a stop.

name: Marino Rocks Lighthouse
reason: No counted source (rule 1); the lighthouse is a short clifftop look from the Marino path.
objection: Could be named by a local guide on the Marino coastal trail.

name: Marino Conservation Park
reason: Parks agency page lists it in Adelaide parks.
objection: Case for: counted source, clifftop walk with sea views. Against: small local reserve, little else names it.

name: Hallett Cove Beach
reason: Wikivoyage mentions Hallett Cove beaches via the Seaford line.
objection: Case for: second-tier beach and the Conservation Park's glacial features nearby. Against: the draw is the Hallett Cove Conservation Park, likely listed separately; beach alone is a transport mention.

name: Kingston Park Coastal Reserve
reason: No counted source (rule 1); a local beach reserve.
objection: Kingston House is historic, but nothing says visitors go in.

name: Port Noarlunga
reason: Wikivoyage mentions the Port Noarlunga line only; known for its jetty and reef snorkelling, but I found no visitor listing in the shard sources.
objection: Case for: classic snorkel jetty and beach. Against: no counted source here beyond transport.

name: Port Noarlunga Reef Aquatic Reserve
reason: Duplicate of Port Noarlunga (snorkel trail off the jetty); no separate counted source.
objection: The reef is the real draw and may deserve to be the named spot rather than the suburb.

name: Christies Beach
reason: No counted source (rule 1); a suburban beach.
objection: Fine beach, but not named by a visitor source.

name: Moana Sands Conservation Park
reason: Rule 3: a small local dune reserve; parks listing only, nothing named to do.
objection: A counted agency page exists.

name: Onkaparinga River National Park
reason: outside the region: belongs to sa-fleurieu (that region covers it).
objection: Parks agency lists it under Adelaide, but the gorge is Fleurieu by the region lines.

name: Brown Hill Creek Recreation Park
reason: Rule 3: a local creek park; agency page only lists it under the Hills.
objection: Has walking trails, but nothing singled out.

name: Sturt Gorge Recreation Park
reason: Parks agency page for the park, gorge walking trails.
objection: Case for: a counted agency page, bushwalking close to the city. Against: local recreation park, no guide singles it out.

name: Shepherds Hill Recreation Park
reason: Rule 3: local suburban park; agency listing only.
objection: Counted listing exists, but no named draw.

name: Glenthorne National Park
reason: Wikivoyage names it as Adelaide's third national park and the parks agency has a page; a national park with walking trails and a visitor offer.
objection: Newly created, limited facilities; the visit may be short.

name: Warriparinga
reason: No counted source in the shard; Kaurna cultural centre and Living Kaurna Cultural Centre on the Sturt River.
objection: Case for: a cultural site visitors can enter. Against: no counted source, local focus.

name: Cobbler Creek Recreation Park
reason: Wikivoyage itself says it is not a major draw (a flood-mitigation dam park).
objection: Parks listing is counted but the guide undercuts it.

name: Angove Conservation Park
reason: Rule 3: a local reserve; no visitor draw named.
objection: Agency listing exists.

name: Para Wirra Conservation Park
reason: Parks agency page: trails and picnic areas in the northern hills.
objection: Case for: a large park with trails an hour from the city. Against: one agency page and no guide singling it out.

name: Classic Jets Fighter Museum
reason: Wikivoyage lists this aviation museum at Parafield with fighter jets.
objection: Case for: indoor museum, 1-2 hours. Against: one source, closed Tuesdays, niche.

name: Salisbury Waterwheel Museum
reason: Wikivoyage itself says 'just a museum' with a restored waterwheel; a minor local museum.
objection: It is a counted listing, but the guide undersells it.

name: Tea Tree Gully Heritage Museum
reason: Rule 3: a small local heritage museum; Wikivoyage listing only.
objection: Open to the public, but nothing sets it apart.

name: National Military Vehicle Museum
reason: Wikivoyage lists it with no description.
objection: Case for: a real museum of military vehicles. Against: a bare listing, one source.

objection: Motorsport venues can host track days, but nothing is permanent for a general visitor.

name: Tramway Museum, St Kilda
reason: No counted source in the shard; tram museum with rides at St Kilda, known locally.
objection: Case for: tram rides, a half-day visit. Against: opens limited days and has no counted source.
